findings: Fixed and verified: all 22 round-one missed definitions (setters, operators, GET/POST, attr_* fields, alias, literal define_method) are now symbols; the five files score 327 expected / 327 correct / 0 missed / 0 spurious. Index status is READY.

Fixed: `include`/`extend`/`prepend` are no longer references (0 edges to Recursive#include, was 18 wrong low edges); no lib file binds to a test file any more; `super` is extracted: 3 of the 4 recall sites bind to the right Helpers method, the 4th (`@params ||= super`) is ambiguous and has no edge.

Most round-one wrong edges are gone (deflater, show_exceptions bytesize, media_type_params, URI_PARSER.escape, lib->test env) but two remain wrong at the same tier: ractorize.rb:11 Request.x_forwarded_proto_priority (high, class-level attr bound to the instance method of Helpers) and spec_request.rb:23 req.env (low).

New wrong edge at HIGH tier in a fresh sample: mock_request.rb:88 `@parser.parse(uri)` where @parser is a URI::Parser (stdlib) is bound to Multipart::Parser.parse with reason 'receiver is named after the type that declares it'. The receiver-named-after-type rule (also behind headers.key? in etag.rb, unclear) can bind a stdlib object at high.

Low-tier reason text 'the only member of this name in the repository' is false whenever an attr_* field of that name exists (req.env: attr_reader :env at request.rb:170 is a symbol, but the edge goes to a test helper NothingMiddleware.env). Also a setter call `req.path_info = x` binds to the getter path_info instead of path_info=, and `@tempfile.path` (stdlib) binds to Request::Helpers#path at low.

Remaining recall gaps: bare identifiers without parentheses used as calls (default arguments `query_parser: default_query_parser`, `x || default_bufsize`) are not extracted; `MultipartInfo.new` on a Struct constant and bare `new(...)` inside a class method are extracted but unresolved; Rack::Utils.default_query_parser.parse_query is ambiguous with no edge.
